title: Session record
description: The front matter of a closed execution episode under .ai/repo/sessions/: what the repository can prove about a stretch of work — its identity and times, the branch and the heads it moved between, the commits it produced, the paths it changed, and the outcome. Written by `majordomus session close` from git and the ledger, never from a transcript: the optional body summarises the work, and this contract has no field for a conversation (ADR 0014, project.never-store-transcripts). The open episode's own state file is a different object with its own schema (session).

schema.description: The format version of this record. A version the tool does not know is refused, never guessed.

session_id.description: The identity, allocated when the episode opened and never reused.

started_at.description: When the episode opened, UTC, RFC 3339.

created_at.description: When the record was written; the closing time.

outcome.description: closed: the episode ended deliberately. interrupted: it stopped without one.

title.description: One line naming the work, for a listing.

task_id.description: The task the episode belonged to, when it belonged to one.

profile.description: The profile the task was worked under.

worker.description: What did the work, as it identified itself: a tool and a model, never a person's name.

branch.description: The branch the episode ran on.

start_head.description: The commit the episode started from.

start_working_tree.description: Whether the working tree was clean or dirty when the episode opened.

working_tree.description: Whether it was clean or dirty when the episode closed.

commits.description: The commits between the two heads, oldest first.

changed_files.description: Repository-relative paths the working tree held changed when the episode closed, classified: what the episode produced, with the paths a declaration calls generated, projected or local left out. changed_files_excluded says how many those were.

changed_files_excluded.description: How many changed paths the classifier kept out of changed_files because a declaration already calls them generated, projected or local. Written on every record, 0 included: it is the list's denominator, and a short list without it cannot be told from a tree that was nearly clean. Its absence marks a record written before the classifier existed.

changed_files_excluded_by.description: Which declaration excluded them, one `<declaration>=<count>` per entry. The names are the declarations lib/changed.sh reads — scope-generated, scope-generated-name, scope-never-read, policy-projection, gitattributes-derived, record-store — so a wrong exclusion names the file to edit. Absent when nothing was excluded.

repository_id.description: The repository the episode ran in, as the tool identifies it.

schema_version.description: Present on records written before the schema identifier; read, never written.

worktree_id.description: A stable identity for the working copy the episode ran in, naming no path: the resolver uses it to tell this checkout's records from another's.

tasks.description: The tasks the episode worked on, by id. Derived from the ledger's own events for this episode; never authored.

issues.description: The issues it moved, by id. Derived from the ledger's own events for this episode; never authored.

milestones.description: The milestones those issues belong to, by id. Derived from the ledger's own events for this episode; never authored.

checkpoints.description: The checkpoints it recorded, by path. Derived from the ledger's own events for this episode; never authored.

handovers.description: The handover records it wrote, by path. Derived from the ledger's own events for this episode; never authored.

decisions.description: The decisions it recorded, by title. Derived from the ledger's own events for this episode; never authored.

questions.description: The questions it opened or resolved. Derived from the ledger's own events for this episode; never authored.

evidence.description: The evidence it attached, as the ledger recorded it. Derived from the ledger's own events for this episode; never authored.
